text: Working with APIs is a fundamental skill for modern developers. When you make an HTTP request to an API, you typically receive data in JSON format, which is easy for both humans and machines to read. Many APIs require authentication, often using an API key, to verify who you are. It's also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain period. If you exceed these limits, the API may temporarily block your access. Finally, always include error handling in your code. Networks can fail, and APIs may return errors, so your program should be prepared to handle these situations gracefully.
